sense: a particular time when something happens

evidence: Traupman 88: for the occasion, in tempus
terms.comment: On this or that occasion is hōc tempore, eō tempore; on the same occasion, at once, ūnō tempore; for the occasion, in tempus (see temporary, moment).
Doubled, it is “on one occasion … on another” (aliās … aliās, Traupman 88).

evidence: Traupman 88: once (on a certain occasion), quōdam diē

terms.comment: Not this sense: occāsiō is the chance or the right moment to do something, not simply a time when something happens (see opportunity).

terms.gloss: as the occasion allows, to suit the occasion
evidence: Sall. Jug. 49.6: pauca prō tempore mīlitēs hortātus (Lewis & Short s.v. hortor)
terms.comment: Sallust’s general says a few words, as much as time allowed. Not “for the time being” (see temporary).

phrases.english: but I’ll write more on another occasion

phrases.latin: adtulit quōdam diē in cūriam praecocem ex eā prōvinciā fīcum
phrases.english: on one occasion he brought into the senate house an early fig from that province

phrases.latin: ō suāvīs epistulās tuās ūnō tempore mihi datās duās!
phrases.english: what lovely letters of yours, two of them handed to me on the same occasion!
